coaching.title: Hills: 6 mi + 1,300 ft, Descending Focus
coaching.message: Calendar has you on the Week 5 vert session — 6 miles, ~1,300 ft, descent-focused. Climbs stay Zone 2 to low Zone 3 (roughly 140-160 bpm); the moment breathing turns ragged, power hike. Steep grades: hands on quads, short steps, tall chest. The real work today is the downhills — Julian Alps will hand you ~2,500m of vert and every meter of it comes back down. Practice quick cadence, light feet, and letting gravity do the work instead of braking. Quads that hold at km 40 are built on days like this. 23 days out, so quality over heroics — finish feeling like you could do it again tomorrow.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Pre-run: 30-50g easy carbs 45-60 min out — banana, toast with honey, or a gel with water. Session is under 90 minutes, so one gel or ~30g carbs mid-run is enough, but use it as gut practice: same product, same timing you'll run in Slovenia. Sodium 700-900 mg/hr — Lima humidity steals more than you think. Post-run inside 45 minutes: 30-40g protein plus 60-80g carbs. Eccentric descending damages muscle fibers hard, so protein today is repair, not optional.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Descending leaves quads trashed even when the run felt easy — expect DOMS tomorrow and plan for it. Ten minutes of eccentric-focused work post-run: quad and hip flexor stretch, calf raises off a step lowering slow, glute bridges. Elevate the legs for 10 minutes tonight. Sleep target 7.5-8 hours. If quads are sharply sore rather than generally achy in 48 hours, back off the next hard session — you're three weeks from the start line and there is nothing left to gain from pushing through damage.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: Twenty-three days. The fitness is built — everything from here is sharpening and protecting it. Today, on the descents, rehearse the exact feeling you want at Kranjska Gora: relaxed shoulders, quiet feet, eyes reading four steps ahead instead of at your toes. Most 50K runners lose their race on the downhills because they never practiced them tired. You're practicing them on purpose. Run it like the last 10K of the Alps, not the first.
